DocumentationNarrative.Body: Command-line tools for BI modeling, conversion, validation, and execution.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: CLI

DocumentationNarrative.Body: Model references for the sanctioned BI metadata workspaces.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Models

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
A typical path can begin with a live system extracted into `MetaSchema`, then move through explicit data-type policy, vault or dimensional architecture, modeled and bound SQL transforms, database structures and deployment assets, data-quality review, pipeline execution, orchestration, and a portable `MetaAnalytics` model projected into Tabular or MultiDimensional form.
Teams compose the sanctioned workspaces that match their architecture. Each handoff remains an inspectable model instance, with the decisions needed for generation, deployment, and execution represented alongside it.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: From source contracts to analytical targets

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The AdventureWorks stack composes 27 workspaces and 29 named operations over a live `AdventureWorks2022` source:
- synchronize the source schema into `MetaSchema`; - generate and deploy Raw and Business Data Vault structures and a dimensional warehouse; - import and strictly bind 53 source-to-Raw, 47 Raw-to-Business, and 20 Business-to-warehouse transforms; - author three pipelines and infer their cross-pipeline orchestration from modeled task and binding evidence; - generate and deploy 176 Data Quality checks; - author portable `MetaAnalytics` semantics, project them into `MetaTabular`, then deploy and process the model.
A clean run reconciled 31,465 orders, 121,317 order lines, and 163 quota rows from source through the warehouse. It reproduced total due `123216786.1159`, line sales `109846381.4250`, quota `95714000.0000`, and zero findings across the promoted Data Quality checks. Repeating the complete ETL preserved the modeled Raw, Business, and warehouse row totals. A processed Tabular deployment returned the same analytical values.
After the create and deployment operations have materialized the stack, execution remains concise:
```powershell cd Demos\AdventureWorksBiStackDemo\AdventureWorksBiStackDemo.MetaMesh meta-mesh operations meta-mesh run --operation run-etl meta-mesh run --operation verify-stack meta-mesh run --operation deploy-tabular meta-mesh run --operation process-tabular ```
The operation names and workspace dependencies are part of the MetaMesh workspace, so the sequence can be inspected and repeated from the model.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: A complete stack in practice

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The sanctioned models divide BI concerns at their natural ownership boundaries:
- **Source and type contracts:** `MetaSchema` captures systems, schemas, tables, fields, keys, and relationships from SQL Server. `MetaDataType` and `MetaDataTypeConversion` carry semantic types and explicit mappings into runtime type systems. - **Data architecture:** `MetaRawDataVault` and `MetaBusinessDataVault` model raw and governed vault structures. `MetaDataWarehouse` models dimensions, facts, grain, business keys, roles, snapshots, bridges, and slowly changing dimensions. Separate implementation workspaces own physical SQL naming, keys, platform columns, defaults, and indexes. - **Transform and database realization:** `MetaTransformScript`, `MetaTransformBinding`, `MetaSql`, and `MetaSqlDeployManifest` carry understood SQL, schema contracts, deployable objects, and controlled deployment. - **Analytical semantics:** `MetaAnalytics` defines portable tables, attributes, hierarchies, measures, aggregation behavior, relationships, perspectives, roles, cultures, and translations before an engine is selected. - **Analytical targets:** `MetaTabular` owns DAX measures, calculation groups, partitions, KPIs, and tabular security. `MetaMultiDimensional` owns cubes, measure groups, MDX, named sets, actions, partitions, and multidimensional security. - **Execution and assurance:** `MetaDataQuality`, `MetaPipeline`, and `MetaOrchestration` turn modeled transform and access evidence into reviewable checks, executable task chains, dependency graphs, synchronization policy, and runtime evidence.
`meta-convert` performs explicit conversions between sanctioned model surfaces, keeping portable intent separate from target-specific implementation details.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Sanctioned model layers

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The runtime tools consume modeled evidence produced by the layers before them:
- **`meta-data-quality`** traverses the typed transform graph to discover reviewable integrity, optionality, fanout, duplicate, join-pattern, and filter-consensus candidates. Binding evidence can restrict generation to transforms whose source and target contracts are already proven. - **`meta-pipeline`** executes modeled transform-backed and external-process tasks, records the exact transform and binding used, and preserves row, batch, timeout, fingerprint, audit, and failure evidence. - **`meta-orchestration`** derives the provable dependency graph from pipeline tasks and bound object reads and writes. Explicit ordering, lock compatibility, synchronization, and failure branches remain modeled policy instead of being buried in scheduler behavior. - **Target CLIs** realize modeled SQL, Tabular, and MultiDimensional workspaces through deployment and processing commands owned by the target model.
Automation therefore follows from explicit contracts. When additional knowledge is required, it enters as modeled policy that engineers and agents can inspect alongside the inferred evidence.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Model-driven execution and evidence

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
SQL has a typed structural representation in the BI stack.
- **`MetaTransformScript`** imports the supported T-SQL surface into a typed syntax graph covering statement roots, query composition, joins, expressions, predicates, grouping, windowing, functions, and bounded mutation statements. The model emits semantically equivalent SQL and proves stability through `SQL -> workspace -> SQL -> workspace` round trips. - **`MetaTransformBinding`** resolves modeled source and target identifiers against explicit `MetaSchema` workspaces. It records rowsets, columns, source objects, target objects, and validation links, and checks target shape and data-type compatibility through sanctioned `MetaDataTypeConversion` policy. - **`MetaSql`** carries deployable database structure, while `MetaSqlDeployManifest` makes source and live fingerprints, schema changes, destructive approvals, and deployment actions explicit before execution.
That shared structure lets later layers reason from transform structure and binding evidence instead of reparsing SQL independently or guessing from text.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: SQL as modeled structure

DocumentationNarrative.Body: `meta-bi` is a model-driven BI engineering stack built on the generic `meta` foundation. It keeps source structures, SQL semantics, transformation contracts, data architecture, deployment assets, execution plans, and analytical targets as typed workspaces that can be inspected, converted, generated, and executed through one model-first foundation.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Overview

DocumentationNarrative.Title: CLI

DocumentationNarrative.Body: Model references for the core metadata foundation.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Models

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`meta` provides the commands used to work with a metadata workspace:
- **Create:** create an empty workspace or create one from another workspace on XML, SQL, or C# (`create`). - **Inspect:** review model and instance state (`status`, `list`, `view`, `query`, `graph`). - **Author:** change model definitions and instance data through model-aware commands (`model ...`, `insert`, `delete`, `bulk-insert`, `instance ...`). - **Refactor:** analyze and apply model changes together with the instance changes they require (`model suggest`, `model refactor ...`). - **Import:** bring SQL metadata or CSV data into a workspace (`import ...`).
Commands use the selected workspace surface for storage and execution.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Meta CLI at a glance

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Workspace-oriented commands use the **current working directory** when `--workspace` is omitted. They do not search parent directories. Use `--workspace <path>` when the target workspace is elsewhere.
Common command behavior:
- successful state changes print `Ok`; - usage and runtime failures explain what prevented the command from continuing and return a non-zero exit code; - mutating commands that expose `--strict` promote warnings to errors.
**Discover the command surface**
```powershell meta help meta help model meta model suggest --help ```
Top-level help lists command groups. Command help then narrows the surface to the relevant usage, arguments, and options.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Command guide

DocumentationNarrative.Body: `meta create --new-workspace <destination> --source-workspace <source> --with-instances --csharp` creates a C# workspace containing the same model and instance graph. Applications can work with its typed model and instance objects directly.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: C# workspace

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Create an XML workspace, add a small model and one row, then create SQL and C# workspaces from the same model and instance graph.
```powershell meta create --new-workspace .\Workspace --xml cd .\Workspace meta model rename-model MetadataModel WorkspaceCatalog meta model add-entity System meta model add-property System SystemName --required true meta insert System 1 --set "SystemName=Enterprise Analytics Platform" meta status meta create --new-workspace ..\SqlWorkspace --source-workspace . --with-instances --sql meta create --new-workspace ..\CsharpWorkspace --source-workspace . --with-instances --csharp ```
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Create workspaces on each surface
One workspace across XML, SQL, and C#

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Metadata is the model that tools operate on. A model defines entity types, their scalar properties, and their relationships. Instance data supplies the records and references for those definitions. A workspace brings the model and its records together for authoring, inspection, refactoring, and execution.
Core terms:
- **Model:** a named set of entity definitions. - **Entity:** a record type, comparable to a table or a POCO type. - **Property:** a scalar attribute on an entity instance. - **Relationship:** a modeled reference from one entity to another. - **Instance:** one identified record of an entity. - **Workspace:** the model and instance data together with the surface-specific storage used to operate on them.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Metadata foundations

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Build the foundation and weave solutions with .NET 8:
```powershell dotnet build Metadata.Framework.sln dotnet build MetaWeave.sln ```
Run a CLI directly from its project during development:
```powershell dotnet run --project Meta/Cli/Meta.Cli.csproj -- help ```
When the CLI output directory is on `PATH`, use the executable name directly:
```powershell meta help ```
On Windows, the `meta`, `meta-weave`, and `meta-docs` project builds also refresh their framework-dependent publish directories under `Cli\bin\publish\win-x64`.
Build the offline installer package with:
```powershell powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Meta\Installer\package-offline.ps1 ```
The default package is framework-dependent and requires the .NET 8 runtime on the target machine. Use `-SelfContained` only when the package must carry its own runtime.
Install the packaged `meta`, `meta-weave`, and `meta-docs` CLIs into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\meta\bin` with:
```powershell Meta\Installer\bin\publish\win-x64-framework-dependent-shared\install-meta.exe ```
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Install and run

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`instances/*.xml` carries the data for a model.
- The document root is the model name, such as `<EnterpriseBIPlatform>`. - Each entity's records appear under a deterministic list container such as `<CubeList>` or `<MeasureList>`. - Each record uses the singular entity name and has an `Id=...` attribute. - Relationship usages are stored as `...Id` attributes. A relationship to `Cube` becomes `CubeId`; a relationship with `role=SourceCube` becomes `SourceCubeId`. - Scalar properties are child elements. A missing element is unset; an empty element is an explicitly empty string.
These rules define the XML instance representation.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Instance XML contract

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The foundation libraries are available as internal NuGet packages:
- `Meta.Core` - `Meta.Adapters` - `MetaWeave.Core`
Build them into the local `.nupkg` feed with:
```powershell .\pack-internal.cmd ```
Downstream repositories consume packages rather than project references back into this repository. That keeps the foundation boundary explicit and prevents downstream changes from silently reaching into core source.
`meta-bi` currently consumes `Meta.Core` from this feed. `MetaWeave.Core` is published alongside it for consumers that need sanctioned cross-model binding services.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Internal packages

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The same model and instance graph can be created, operated on, and moved between XML, SQL, and C# workspaces without changing its meaning.
Choose the surface for the work at hand:
- **XML** is suited to authoring, review, branching, and merging. - **SQL** is suited to database-native constraints, queries, and set-based changes to large instance sets. - **C#** is suited to typed application and service code.
The surface changes storage and execution. It does not change the model or the records it describes.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Why isomorphic metadata

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
`model.xml` declares the schema of a metadata workspace: which entities exist, which scalar properties they carry, and how they relate.
A model has one `<Model name=...>` root and follows a small set of rules:
- `<Entity name=Cube>` defines a record type; every entity has an implicit `Id`. - `<PropertyList>` contains scalar text fields. Properties are required by default; `isRequired=false` makes a property optional. - `<RelationshipList>` contains references to other entities. Relationships are required by default. - A relationship role is used when more than one relationship targets the same entity and the references need distinct meanings. - XML instance containers use the deterministic `<EntityName>List` convention.
These rules define the XML model representation.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Model XML contract

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
The foundation is delivered through five command-line tools:
- **`meta`** creates and operates on model and instance workspaces across XML, SQL, and C# surfaces. It authors and inspects models, refactors model and instance data, and imports external metadata. - **`meta-cli`** defines command grammars and provides the shared parser, help, workspace access, and handler runtime used by the suite. - **`meta-weave`** defines and validates sanctioned property bindings across models, then materializes those bindings when one combined workspace is needed. - **`meta-docs`** combines CLI and model reference data with authored technical documentation, then merges and renders the public reference. - **`meta-mesh`** declares the workspaces involved in a repository workflow and the ordered executable steps that operate on them.
BI-specific sanctioned models and command-line tools live in the separate `meta-bi` repository.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Foundation command-line tools

DocumentationNarrative.Body: `meta create --new-workspace <destination> --source-workspace <source> --with-instances --sql` creates a SQL workspace containing the model and instance graph. SQL provides database-native storage, foreign-key enforcement, queries, and set-based updates for large instance sets.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: SQL workspace

DocumentationNarrative.Body: `meta` is the foundation CLI for creating and operating model and instance workspaces. It carries one workspace between XML, SQL, and C# surfaces while preserving the model and its records.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Overview

DocumentationNarrative.Body: XML workspaces fit naturally into Git. Model definitions, instance data, and refactors remain structured, so a change can be reviewed as metadata rather than as an opaque file-format rewrite. Stable ordering and consistent encoding keep diffs focused on the change itself.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Version-control friendly workspaces

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
A workspace is the unit that commands create, inspect, change, and move between surfaces. It contains a model, its instance data, and the storage configuration required by the selected surface.
The workspace API keeps those storage details behind one boundary, so a command can work with the metadata without taking ownership of files, tables, or typed object graphs.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Workspace contract

DocumentationNarrative.Body:
Commands open a workspace through its selected surface and operate on that workspace through one API. Callers do not need to manage XML files, SQL tables, or C# object graphs as separate product concepts.
An operation may stay native to its surface when that is useful, such as a set-based SQL update. When an algorithm needs the complete graph, the workspace API can materialize it without changing the model or instance semantics.
DocumentationNarrative.Title: Workspace surfaces and execution
